value.title: Builder warning-first guidance: staged composition and startup cutover

value.principles: Keep acts thin and services port-injected. Ownership path comparisons return data, never permission failures. Reuse builderOwnsPath and logical POSIX paths; use one typed warning format, persist observations in receipts, and preserve actual check results separately. No amendment code. First increment keeps the coupled composition writer/reader/schema change together; subsequent startup and delivery changes reuse that warning seam.
value.composition_root: harness/cli/src/acts/builder.ts registers commands and renders existing envelopes; services/builder/composition-service.ts owns import and verify side effects.
contracts: Increment 1: CompositionReceipt.warnings is an optional array for historical read compatibility; new receipts write an array. Each OwnershipWarning contains exact file, owning_unit (one unit ID, or unmapped), and stage (import or verify). Multiple mapped owners yield separate rows. Scalar owner labels remain visible in the standard DD renderer; this is observation, never authorization.

Import warnings describe pre-import PM integration; verify preserves import-stage warnings and replaces verify-stage warnings for the current candidate so retries do not accumulate stale current-state warnings. Owning units derive from the complete guide map, using existing prefix matching.

The path comparison still propagates actual Git/ancestry failures with cause and fix. Crossing a mapped ownership path is always a successful comparison result. Real build/test failures remain red and persist warnings beside failure evidence.
Reviewers read composition warnings alongside the artifact. No warning-resolution decision, declared_by field, policy flag, receipt mutation gate or additional review prerequisite is added.

Later increments: reuse the same comparison for on-track and delivery; replace acknowledgement-dependent release with one optional self-check. Final CLI grammar will be fixed before those changes; do not ship speculative commands in increment 1.
harness builder self-check <packet> --sha256 <expected-packet-digest>; no builder ack alias

selfCheckBuilderPacket(deps: BuilderDeps, input: SelfCheckInput): Promise<BuilderResult<SelfCheckReport>> in self-check-service.ts; all inspection mismatches become a successful report with BuilderIssue[] warnings, not refusal.

{packet, expected:{packet_sha256,root?,source_sha?}, observed:{packet_sha256?,root?,source_sha?}, warnings:BuilderIssue[]}; no write or native transport operation. Each warning names cause and corrective next_action.

Packet.source_sha optional for reading historical packets, populated on every new packet. nonce remains a correlation value only. canary optional for reading history, never produced or demanded by current flow.

New DispatchReceipt.delivery optional transport outcome with message_id/outcome/recorded_at. Persist native observation before send, then CAS the observed work-packet delivery. It is a transport fact, not acknowledgement/permission. Retired acknowledgement/release remain historical decode fields only.

Read explicitly selected bounded regular packet, measure digest even if mismatched, compare actual repository root and HEAD with packet workspace and source_sha. For a historical packet lacking source_sha, use its in-root digest-bound baseline. Missing/unreadable/invalid packet/baseline or Git inspection yields warnings and no pretend success observation. Do not read arbitrary baseline paths outside the checkout. No clock window, root challenge, cleanliness/metadata veto, native seat handshake or state write.

Bind exact current packet, dispatch and external allocation digests to delivery peer/workspace/source/unit. Validate root/branch and baseline ancestry before mutation. Compare packet.source_sha when present. Do not consult AckReceipt, acknowledgement, release outcome, delivery outcome, nonce/time-window or canary. Existing coder path-ownership warning conversion is checkpoint 3, not this change.

FsPort.readBytesNoFollow(path, {maxBytes, root?}) optionally uses the existing bounded opened-file/confinement reader for exact packet-byte hashing. One-argument callers keep their existing behavior. Baseline reads supply the actual repository root; invalid UTF-8 remains observed bytes plus a warning, not a decoded-text digest claim.

value.rationale: One canonical native Builder plan/workspace remains PM-owned. For increment 2, three tool subagents implement disjoint source slices against the PM-owned API/schema contract; they are not Builder-dispatched native units or separate native clones. Their code is integrated and independently reviewed as one artifact; no native fleet proof is claimed.

value.path: Subsequent checkpoint: The implementation guide retains units[].paths and read maps, and packets still carry the assigned unit, its job and observable done conditions; these maps guide work rather than granting write permission.
compose import/verify -> mapped warning list -> composition receipt and reviewer

Subsequent checkpoint: Coder delivery and advancement/import report out-of-map history as the same warning list, including mapped owning unit(s) or an explicit unmapped result, and continue when actual integrity checks pass. No remaining ownership-only check in Builder may refuse.

Subsequent checkpoint: A self-serve on-track command works in the coder clone and on the PM integration delta, including selected committed and current work as documented; it returns the same comparison and warnings with exit 0, performs no release/import/approval and does not change source.

Subsequent checkpoint: The packet begins with plain-language ownership/read map, job and done conditions before mechanics. Its embedded unit remains available; first-use instructions lead directly to useful work rather than acknowledgement ceremony.

Subsequent checkpoint: A coder can run one advisory self-check of expected clone, source commit and packet digest. Mismatch, drift or normal startup metadata yields named observations/warnings and repair advice rather than a work-release gate; there is no required second receipt, second nonce or clock window.

Subsequent checkpoint: Dispatch, delivery, import, advance and review no longer depend on pre-work/post-release acknowledgement receipt IDs, phase nonces, canary challenge or plus/minus-five-second timing to authorize work; old records remain readable and need no replay or fabricated upgrade.

Subsequent checkpoint: At import, wrong tree/commit lineage, forged or mismatched delivery/packet evidence, duplicate peer and rewritten baseline still refuse before an incorrect composition mutation. Each integrity refusal names the actual cause and corrective next step; legitimate descendant source and evidence-only commits retain their supported path.
compose import/verify -> mapped warning list -> composition receipt and reviewer

Subsequent checkpoint: The supported runtime, help, schemas, docs, skills and examples contain no amendment requirement or competing two-receipt startup path. PR #200 remains closed without merge; no alias or legacy gate revives its declaration design.

Subsequent checkpoint: A real CLI/Git consumer scenario demonstrates map-first dispatch, one optional advisory self-check, cross-map coder/PM edits, warning-preserving import/composition, independent review and receipt-only archival re-observation; contrasting integrity failures still refuse and existing historical evidence remains unmodified.

value.name: PM warning-first integration
value.responsibility: PM integrates the three approved increments. Current checkpoint uses three tool helpers with disjoint source maps; PM owns shared API/schema/fixtures, real smoke, final validation and canonical evidence. No native coder allocations or their handshakes are fabricated.
value.interface: Existing composeBuilderUnits returns Stored<CompositionReceipt>; warnings extend that receipt as optional historical-compatible data. No public command changes in increment 1.
value.notes: Paths are the map under the ruling, not an authority gate. No coder release or two-receipt ceremony is necessary for this solo first increment.

value.note: One isolated plan checkout with file-owned tool subagents, not native coder clones. Shared contracts and validation are PM-owned; no native acknowledgement ceremony is used to implement its removal.

value.description: Type-check public receipt and injected service contracts
Behavioral composition/act/contract regressions, including continued proof and retained integrity failures
Real CLI/Git source smoke; extend for warning-bearing committed composition before claiming AC proof
Installed package CLI smoke; run after building the intended source

steps: Implement and verify the receipt contract and composition warning paths with the PM as the only source owner.
Run existing targeted tests with changed warning behavior and unchanged integrity contrasts; exercise real Git/CLI, including warnings on failed checks.
Commit the exact source, obtain independent review, and run the full repository gate. Publish increment 1 separately; send PR and exact head to the prime for merge/activation confirmation.
Do not mark later packet/self-check/delivery acceptance complete. Start subsequent increments from the approved staged order; preserve both source and red evidence from consumers.

Increment 2: PM owns shared APIs/schemas/fixtures and real CLI proof; the startup producer, delivery consumer and source-guidance helpers edit disjoint source areas. No tests/builds while concurrent edits are active. Integrate once, run source/packed smoke and all-scope checks, obtain exact-source independent review, publish separate PR for prime release confirmation.

value.when: Independent design/source review before publishing increment 1 and each subsequent checkpoint; PM cannot self-approve.
inputs: Exact source SHA, plan/guide and recorded warning/check evidence
Warning records identify file and owning units, or unmapped
Original integrity fixtures and real-Git smoke output; no claim of live fleet execution from tests
proof: Existing independent review must assess the actual bytes and warning evidence; no new warning-approval gate
Separate static review, test proof, CLI smoke and deployed consumer receipt claims

Increment 1 uses independent tool-driven source review; it does not claim a native Builder review receipt or provider/model attestation. No new role profile is asserted for an unobserved reviewer runtime.

value.check: Contrast ownership warning with failed ancestry and failed check; warnings cannot hide these failures.

value.check: Stage-aware warning replacement; retry and red-check persistence assertions.

value.check: Schema-backed warning list plus readable receipt output and named reviewer input.

value.text: Staged rollout is misrepresented as the complete new lifecycle.
